maria_nguyen: Quick async — need confirmation on /v1/generate routing behavior. I noticed when a model ID is unavailable in a region the platform used to fallback to the same model in another region, then to different model variants. After the recent routing change I'm seeing it pick a lower-tier variant in-region first. Is that intended? If so, is that contract-stable for users?

zach_garcia: That's expected for the new default: prefer same-region lower-tier instead of cross-region. The idea was latency-first. But we didn't publish a formal contract change. Do we have a spec update?

kyle_chen: We didn't update API surface. Current behavior is implementation detail. But I agree we need explicit contract. Two options: (1) documented default (latency-first), (2) introduce a param to control fallback strictness. Thoughts?

maria_nguyen: Option 2 sounds safer. Can we add `routing.strict_model` or `strict_model=true` that returns 404-like error when exact model unavailable? We also need a soft deprecation path for clients relying on old behavior.

kyle_chen: Proposal: new boolean `strict_model` (default false). If true, return HTTP 424 with body {"error":"model_unavailable","served_model":null}. If false, current fallback logic applies. Add `served_model` in response always to make contract explicit.

sophia_lee: I like `served_model` in response. Also add `fallback_chain` array for debugging when not strict. Example response snippet:

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{
  "id": "req_...",
  "served_model": "redwood-v1-medium",
  "fallback_chain": ["redwood-v1-large (unavailable in region) ", "redwood-v1-medium (served)"]
}
```

zach_garcia: Small nit: don't expose internal availability reasons verbatim. `fallback_chain` should be sanitized, e.g. ["redwood-v1-large","redwood-v1-medium"], plus a `reasons` map in logs only.

maria_nguyen: Agreed. Also need a region hint param - `region_hint` and `tier_hint` were already in API. Are these still respected by the new routing order?

kyle_chen: Yes: precedence will be: explicit `model` exact match in `region_hint` -> same-region lower-tier variants -> cross-region same-tier -> cross-region lower-tier. If `strict_model=true` we short-circuit after first step and return 424.

sophia_lee: Can we add a compatibility header `X-Routing-Behavior: legacy|latency-first|strict` so clients can opt into legacy behavior while migrating? It can mirror the `routing_behavior` enum in the request body.

kyle_chen: Implementable. Plan: add `routing_behavior` enum: ["legacy","latency_first","strict"]. Default `latency_first`. `strict` == `strict_model=true` behavior. `legacy` preserves previous cross-region preference. We will also add `served_model` and `fallback_chain` (sanitized) to responses.

maria_nguyen: Excellent. Does this require any DB migrations or config flags for Dedicated/Private customers?

kyle_chen: No DB changes. It's routing logic change + response fields. Dedicated instances need a rollout toggle; I'll add a feature flag and a canary to 10% traffic.

sophia_lee: I'll update docs + OpenAPI spec. Tests: add unit tests for the four precedence paths and an integration test verifying X-Routing-Behavior header is set when `routing_behavior` present.

zach_garcia: PR pls: #3245 (draft). @kyle_chen can you add the flag + smoke tests? @sophia_lee once docs updated I'll send a short PSA to integrations slack.

kyle_chen: On it. I'll also add migration note in release notes about `served_model` addition and `strict` mode. Marking for code review: @maria_nguyen can you review the API contract doc when ready?

maria_nguyen: Yup. I'll review tomorrow. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

infra-bot: deployment scheduled: routing-service v3.12.0-canary -> 10% traffic at 2025-08-14T22:00:00Z

sophia_lee: Added docs PR #460 in docs repo. Linking in the PR now.

kyle_chen: Updating the milestone and test plan in the PR.

maria_nguyen: Cool, closing loop here. If anyone sees behavioral regressions in canary pls ping in #incidents.
